subject: Performance RFI: concurrency, cache effects, and fallback behavior
messages:
From: Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@mercuryfin.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Mercury R&D Team <rd@mercuryfin.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: Mercury RFI: performance breakdown and methodology

Markus —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're finalizing the performance section of our RFP and need a compact but reproducible set of results from Redwood showing how the platform behaves for our primary workloads. The RFP workbook (attached) calls out three specific areas we need you to address:

1) Tail latency decomposition across concurrency (1, 8, 32, 128 concurrent requests) at sequence lengths 64 / 256 / 1024 tokens; we want p50/p90/p95/p99 and full latency histogram for each combo.
2) Effect of prefix/KV cache (cold vs warm) and how cache hit-rate correlates with observed batching and latency under mixed short+long request mixes.
3) Behavior and runbook for graceful fallback under capacity constraints — specifically: what triggers fallback to quantized model variants, how you measure correctness regressions, and how routing changes are effected during a step-down.

Deliverables: a short methodology doc, the run matrix (CSV) with exact configs you used, and a single-page summary with acceptance criteria (what counts as pass/fail for our SLA).

Can you confirm the exact test harness you will run (synthetic driver vs replay), what telemetry you'll provide (raw traces vs aggregated metrics), and an estimated ETA for deliverables? We're hoping to include this in our scoring next week.

Attachments: mercury_rfi_v2.xlsx

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Reeves
Director, Platform Engineering — Mercury Financial
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@mercuryfin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T13:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Mercury RFI: performance breakdown and methodology

Tom —

Appreciate the detail. We can absolutely provide the artifacts you requested. At a high level, here's what we propose and why it maps to the RFP scoring rubric:

Summary of proposed approach (short):
- Test harness: two-parallel strategy — (A) deterministic synthetic driver (JMeter + custom token-level client) to sweep concurrency and sequence length in controlled steps; (B) optional replay of sanitized production traces if you provide them (preferred for real-world mix).
- Telemetry: we'll deliver raw per-request traces (timestamps, model-version, batch-id, kvcache_hit boolean), aggregated histograms (p50/p90/p95/p99), GPU/core-level utilization traces, batching histograms (batch size vs latency), and end-to-end throughput curves.
- Cache experiments: cold starts (no warm prefix state), warm state with at-scale repeated prefixes, and intermediate warmups; we'll report hit-rate vs tail-latency correlation.
- Fallback/runbook: we will simulate capacity pressure and show both automatic graceful fallback to a quantized variant and routing to a lower-cost region/model (if configured). We will include automated quality checks (BLEU-like heuristics + a small human-evaluated prompt set) and threshold gates for circuit-breaker activation.

Acceptance criteria we recommend (draft):
- p95 <= 300ms for sequence=64 at concurrency<=32 for hosted offering to meet interactive SLA.
- p99 <= 800ms for sequence=256 under concurrency<=8 for dedicated.
- Quality delta between full FP16 and quantized variant <= 3% on our short eval set (we provide prompts).
- KV cache warm hit-rate >= 80% reduces p95 by >= 30% in mixed short-heavy traffic.

Attachments included: redwood-mf-rfi-response.pdf (methodology and sample configs) and run-matrix-20260810.csv (proposed configs).

Next steps:
- Marissa, Kimberly: please see the run plan in the CSV and confirm resource ops (GPU types, job duration) and default metric collection.
- Tom: confirm whether you want replay traces or we'll proceed with synthetic runs. If synthetic, confirm the traffic mix percentages for Short (<=64) / Medium (65-256) / Long (257-1024).

ETA: If we proceed with synthetic only, initial deliverables (methodology + first run matrix + summary) by 2026-08-17. Full CSV of raw traces + final pass by 2026-08-24 after three run iterations.

Thanks —
Markus Klein
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Mercury RFI: performance breakdown and methodology

Adding operational details and reminders for the runbook:

Planned synthetic load profile (proposal):
- Phase 0 (baseline): 15 minutes at concurrency=1 across seq lengths 64/256/1024 to capture cold-start behavior.
- Phase 1 (ramp): linear step-up 1 -> 8 -> 32 over 45 minutes for each sequence length, hold each step 10 minutes and collect histograms.
- Phase 2 (stress): short bursts to concurrency=128 for 3x 2-minute windows spaced 5 minutes apart to exercise tail/backpressure.
- Phase 3 (mixed steady): 2 hours with a 60/30/10 Short/Medium/Long distribution to emulate production.

Metrics to capture (must-collect):
- Per-request: request_id, start_ts, end_ts, model_variant, sequence_length, kvcache_hit boolean, batch_id.
- Aggregates: bucketed latency histograms, batch-size distribution, GPU util, memory footprint, network egress, retry/fallback events.
- Quality checks: for any fallback run we capture a 100-sample human-reviewed set plus our auto-delta scorer.

Log retention and format: raw traces will be provided as compressed CSVs (schema in run-matrix CSV). Aggregates in Prometheus-style metrics and p95/p99 histograms as JSON.

Observability checkpoints:
- Canary checkpoint (after first ramp) to validate instrumentation and sanity.
- Post-run regression job to compute quality delta and generate the final pass/fail table.

Attachments: load-profiles.yaml (profiles for the driver)

Note: we recommend running the cache-warm experiments with a synthetic prefix generator to avoid sharing customer secrets or production tokens. If Mercury can sanitize traces with prefix hashing, we can do the replay path as well.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@mercuryfin.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Mercury R&D Team <rd@mercuryfin.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T17:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Mercury RFI: performance breakdown and methodology

Markus / Marissa —

Appreciate the plan, looks solid. A few clarifications we need before you run:

1) Please separate results into three columns in your final matrix: Hosted (Redwood cloud), Dedicated (reserved GPU pool), Private (VPC/on-prem simulation). We want to see where each offering sits for the same run config.
2) For fallback behavior: can you provide a deterministic stepdown policy example? We care about the sequence of actions (scale down batch size -> enable quantized variant -> route to lower-cost region) and how long each step takes under sustained pressure.
3) For quality checks: we will provide a small curated 200-prompt set. Will you run those through both FP16 and quantized variants and include the comparison CSV?
4) Canary plan: we prefer a short canary on a dedicated slice of our production traffic (1% sample) after the synthetic windows. Can you outline the rollback conditions?

If you can confirm these items and deliver the initial artifacts by 2026-08-17 as proposed, we'll keep Mercury's RFP scoring on track.

Thanks,
Tom
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@mercuryfin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-14T09:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Mercury RFI: performance breakdown and methodology

Tom —

Confirming the plan and answering your points inline:  

1) Hosted / Dedicated / Private columns: yes — we'll run the same synthetic configs against all three deployment types. Private will be a VPC-on-cloud deployment (we'll simulate on equivalent HW) unless you schedule an on-prem window; results will be labelled clearly.

2) Deterministic stepdown policy (example):
- Trigger: sustained 5-minute p99 > 1.5x target or GPU util > 92% for 3 consecutive mins.
- Step 1 (0-30s): increase request queuing and tighten batch window (reduces latency variance). Log event: STEP_ADJUST_BATCH.
- Step 2 (30-90s): enable automatic fallback to quantized variant for non-critical routes (route tag=best-effort). Log event: STEP_ENABLE_QUANT.
- Step 3 (90-180s): redirect new requests to a lower-cost region (if policy allows) and reduce concurrency caps. Log event: STEP_REGION_FALLBACK.
- Observability: each step emits structured events; the automated circuit-breaker will open if quality delta > configured threshold for 2 consecutive checks.

We will include a trace example in the canary-playbook.md that shows the timing and logs for a simulated pressure event.

3) Quality checks: yes — run the 200-prompt set you provide on FP16 and on quantized variant; we'll include side-by-side CSV with delta metrics and a human-review summary when applicable.

4) Canary rollback conditions (proposal):
- Any single metric crossing: p99 > 2x target OR error-rate increase > 0.5% absolute triggers immediate rollback to pre-canary routing.
- Quality regression: if automated quality delta > 5% on the 200-prompt set, hold and rollback.
- Manual abort: Mercury Ops can abort the canary at any time; we will also auto-abort on any data-exfiltration detection (we'll not run with production PII).

Deliverables timeline (final):
- 2026-08-17: methodology PDF + run-matrix CSV + proposed short-run summary (synthetic).
- 2026-08-20: first full-run synthetic CSVs + aggregated dashboards (Prometheus/JSON).
- 2026-08-24: replay runs (if you provide sanitized traces) + final deliverable (full raw traces + summary + canary-playbook).

We'll proceed with synthetic only unless we hear you prefer replay. Planning: canary date (if all goes well) 2026-08-24 -> we'll reserve a 2-hour window that day; final report by EOD 2026-08-24.

Attachments: canary-playbook.md, mercury-performance-matrix-20260824.csv

Best —
Markus Klein
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
